description:
GOAL

Make enum_reduce_suspend prove the semantic suspension boundary without depending on allocator-order function numbering.

SIGNAL

Adding two unrelated functions to lib/enum.fz changes the rendered continuation from #fn<125/0> to #fn<127/0> on interp, JIT, and AOT. Allocation counters and behavior are unchanged. The fixture prose already says schema/function numbering is not semantic, but expected.txt and expected.interp.txt still pin the number. The prose also carries stale historical IDs and tactical implementation notes instead of a durable statement of the behavior under test.

STRATEGY

Pattern-match the suspended result into a stable summary, capture allocation stats before resuming, then invoke the returned zero-arity function and assert its completed reduction result. Remove the historical commentary. Keep the allocation goldens that prove a real heap closure exists and preserve the separate interpreter/native counts.

ACCEPTANCE

- No golden or fixture prose names a numeric function ID.
- The fixture proves the suspended accumulator, the closure allocation boundary, and the resumed result.
- interp, JIT, and AOT legs pass before any dependent library surface is pushed.
- The full fixture matrix remains green.
title: Enum suspend fixture pins a nonsemantic function ID
